description:
Found by the #423 probes (s424), PRE-EXISTING and independent of #423's fix.

    open my $fh, '<', '/etc/hostname' or die;
    print ref($fh), "|", ref(\$fh), "|", "$fh";

    perl : GLOB|REF|GLOB(0x55...)
    PCL  :     |SCALAR|GLOB(0x1)

PCL represents a lexical filehandle as a RAW STREAM inside the box (perl makes
it a glob ref).  `stringify-value` has a `streamp` arm and prints GLOB(0xADDR)
for it (correct), but nothing else does:

  * `p-ref`'s payload cond has arms for box / hash / vector / function /
    typeglob / regex -- none for `streamp`, so it falls through to `(t "")`.
  * `%scalar-holds-ref-p` lists typeglob but not streamp, so a referent box
    holding a stream answers SCALAR instead of REF.
  * `%p-ref-string` has no stream arm either (its box-referent branch reaches
    the SCALAR default).

So the STRING says "this is a glob ref" and ref() says "this is not a
reference" -- the #163 rule (the word and the number and ref() agree) broken
for exactly one payload kind.  s424 fixed the typeglob member of this family
(#423) and deliberately did NOT widen to streams: `ref($fh) eq 'GLOB'` becoming
true changes behaviour in every IO path (lib/IO/Handle.pm:390 is
`if (ref($fd) && "$fd" =~ /GLOB\(/o)` -- perl takes that branch for a lexical
handle, PCL does not), so it needs the io/ companion leg of its own.

FIX SHAPE (one rule, three readers -- the same three s424 touched):
  streamp (and %p-socket-p?) joins the reference payload kinds in `p-ref`
  ("GLOB"), `%scalar-holds-ref-p` (a referent holding a stream ? REF) and
  `%p-ref-string` (GLOB(0xADDR), which stringify-value already prints).
  Probe first: ref($fh) / ref(\$fh) / "$fh" / reftype($fh) / 0+$fh /
  `bless $fh` / a closed handle / a socket / a dirhandle, plus IO::Handle's
  new_from_fd path, vs perl.
BAR: the io/ companion leg (tools/run-perl-suite.pl --dir io) A/B'd, plus the
  full sweep -- `ref($fh)` is reachable from every file that opens a handle.
title: A lexical filehandle is not a GLOB to ref(): ref($fh) is "" and ref(\$fh) is SCALAR where perl says GLOB / REF (the stream referent has no arm)
